20.13. \uline{Elementary morphisms and the theorem of} M. \uline{Artin}.

\uline{Definition} 13.1. A morphism $f:X\hand{\to} Y$ of preschemes is called an “\var{\xout{elem}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_075-v0001}
elementary morphism” if X is \var{\xout{a}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_075-v0002} Y-isomorphic to a prescheme of the form
$X' - Z$, where $X'\hand{\to} X$ is a smooth projective morphism with connected geometric
fibers\var{\xout{\unsure{,}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_075-v0003} of dimension 1, and where Z is a closed subprescheme
of X', \var{\xout{étale over}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_075-v0004} such that the morphism $Z\hand{\to} Y$ is étale, surjective, and
of constant degree. A morphism is called \var{\xout{\unsure{multip-elementary}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_075-v0005} poly-elementary
if it is a composite of elementary morphisms. A prescheme X
over a field k is called poly-elementary (over k) if the structural
morphism $X\hand{\to} \mathrm{Spec}(k)$ is poly-elementary.

{\microtypesetup{protrusion=false}\uline{Theorem} 13.2. \var{\inserted[typed]{(M.Artin)}}{(M.Artin)}{insertion}{ega25_25_075-v0006} Let X be a \var{\inserted[typed]{geom. irred.}}{geom. irred.}{insertion}{ega25_25_075-v0007} prescheme over a \var{\inserted[typed]{perfect infinite}}{perfect infinite}{insertion}{ega25_25_075-v0008} field k, x a smooth point
of X; then x has a fundamental system of poly-elementary open
neighborhoods.\par}

14. \uline{Conical projections}.

NB We have already used conical projections on various
\var{\margin{$\|$}}{\placedmargin{$\|$}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_084-v0001}occasions, in particular at the end of no. 8, the formulation of 10.4 and elsewhere, and
the following sorites should probably come instead at the beginning of the paragraph,
and possibly in the auxiliary “Grassma\unsure{n}nian” paragraph.
Let $C = P(F)$ be a linear subvariety of $P(E)=P$, of relative
dimension $r-m-1$ \var{\xout{in}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_084-v0002} over $S$\var{\inserted[typed]{i.e. of codimension $m+1$ in $P$}}{ i.e. of codimension $m+1$ in $P$}{insertion}{ega25_25_084-v0003}, so $F$ is a quotient of $E$, loc free of
rank $r-m$, $F=E/G$, where $G$ is loc free of rank $m+1$. We defined
algebraically in Chap II a morphism
\[ p_C : P - C = P(E) - P(E/G) \hand{\longrightarrow} P(G) , \]
which we shall interpret geometrically, and which will be called
(in view of the following description) the \uline{conical projection} with center $C$.
(NB We assume $r-m-1$ lies between $-1$ and $r-1$, i.e. $m$ between $0$
and $r$, with no further restriction.) For this, let us begin by interpreting \var{\xout{\unsure{Q(G)}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_084-v0004} $P(G)$
as a sub\var{\inserted[typed]{pre}}{pre}{insertion}{ega25_25_084-v0005}scheme\var{\inserted[typed]{closed}}{ closed}{insertion}{ega25_25_084-v0006} in $\mathrm{Grass}^m(P)= \mathrm{Grass}_{r-m+1}(P)$, by means of the evident homomorphism
of functors
\[ \var{\xout{\unsure{Gr|G}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_084-v0007}\ P(G) \hand{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{Grass}_{r-m+1}(E) \]
obtained by considering, for each invertible quotient $G/G'$ of $G$, the
locally free Module of rank $(r-m)+1$ $E/G'$ of $E$ (and the same after
any base change). The preceding homomorphism of functors is a
\uline{monomorphism}, and since the first is proper over $S$ and the second separated,
it is a closed immersion. \var{\xout{\unsure{(}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_084-v0008}More generally, we should make explicit
the closed immersions of the Grassmannians of $G$, i.e. of $P(G)$,
into those of \var{\inserted{$E$ i.e. of}}{$E$ i.e. of}{insertion}{ega25_25_084-v0009} $P=P(E)$. \var{\xout{\unsure{Here,}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_084-v0010} The image\var{\inserted[typed]{(in the functor sense)}}{ (in the functor sense)}{insertion}{ega25_25_084-v0011} of the resulting morphism consists of
the linear subvarieties \var{\xout{of M}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_084-v0012} $L$\var{\inserted[typed]{of the desired dimension}}{ of the desired dimension}{insertion}{ega25_25_084-v0013} of $P$ that \uline{contain} $C$. Denoting
this image by $Q(C)$ in the case at hand (i.e. for the dimensions
specified above), and identifying $P(G)$ with $Q(C)$, the conical
projection morphism
\[ p_C : P - C \hand{\longrightarrow} Q(C) \hand{\subset} \mathrm{Grass}^m(P) \]
\tnote{25-084-1}{Conical projection renders projection conique. The subscript r-m+1 in the displayed Grassmannians and the source's description of E/G' as a Module of E are retained. Kif kif is rendered the same.}

We shall give another interpretation of this morphism, in

\[ q':q^{-1}(X-f^{-1}(C)) \hand{\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }} X - f^{-1}(C) \ , \]

\uline{Corollary} 14.2. Suppose X of dimension m and f:X$\hand{\to}$P finite\var{\inserted[typed]{(resp quasi-finite)}}{ (resp quasi-finite)}{insertion}{ega25_25_088-v0013}; then
the morphism $p_{C_{\hand{\unsure{\eta|y}}}} : X_{k(\hand{\unsure{\eta|y}})} \hand{\unsure{\longrightarrow|\relbar}} Q(C_{\hand{\unsure{\eta|y}}})$ is finite surjective (resp. quasi-finite

\uline{Corollary} 14.3. Under the conditions of 14.1 a), if X is Cohen–Macaulay,

$\overset{\hand{\sim}}{F}(C_{\hand{\unsure{\eta|y}}})$ is CM (and a fortiori flat) relative to Q(C$_{\hand{\unsure{\eta|y}}}$).

statement given with the assertion (in general false) that p$_C$ itself is a

Thus dim E \hand{$<$} N = dim $\unsure{P|G}$, hence $E_{\hand{\unsure{\eta|y}}} = \hand{\emptyset}$, and a fortiori $X_{\hand{\unsure{\eta|y}}}$ is smooth\var{\inserted{over $k(\unsure{\eta|y})$}}{ over $k(\unsure{\eta|y})$}{insertion}{ega25_25_095-v0001}\hand{.}
This point established, we immediately conclude that the evident
variants of 2.12. to 2.18. are valid in the present context.

The passage in no. 4 from a generic section to a general section
and the developments of no. 5 are evidently valid in the present
context (but are to such an extent tautologies or repetitions\var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_095-v0002} of
par.8,9,12 \var{\xout{)}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_095-v0003} that one hesitates to state them formally). Likewise the
developments of 7.1., valid in any case if k is \var{\xout{infinite}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_095-v0004} alg closed
(and even if k is merely infinite, if we suppose G rational over k),
and the special cases 7.2., 7.3.; as for the result\var{\xout{s}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_095-v0007} 7.4. \var{\xout{and 7.5.}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_095-v0008}
\var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_095-v0009}it is evidently \var{\inserted[typed]{an application}}{an application}{insertion}{ega25_25_095-v0010} of a special nature \var{\inserted[typed]{of}}{of}{insertion}{ega25_25_095-v0011} \var{\xout{to}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_095-v0012} the situation of hyperplane
sections. As I have said, nos. 3 and 6 depend on the extension
of Zariski's th.

It would remain also to extend the results of no. 8 (taken up again in
no. 12), which may in this way take on a more appealing form.
I even advise you to begin by writing up these results in this framework,
trying to go as far as possible in this direction. I have
the impression that we must be able to recover at least everything that is not a
direct consequence of 8.7. c) (and we could even try
to extract axiomatic conditions making a variant of
8.7. c) work. I confine myself to these recommendations, but am ready to return to them
in more detail if you have particular difficulties.

\unsure{mined by these conditions, as is $\underline{M}_i$ up to unique isomorphism.}
\unsure{Corollary 1.2.} \unsure{--- If we make no hypothesis on the rank of E, S}
\unsure{decomposes canonically as a sum of three opens $S'$, $S''$, $S'''$ such that on}
\unsure{$S'$, $S''$, $S'''$, the rank of $\underline{E}$ is 0, 1, $\geq 2$. Then the determination of}

\unsure{$f^{-1}(S')$ is empty, hence its Picard group is zero.}
\uline{\unsure{Corollary 1.3.}} \unsure{Under the conditions of 1.1, suppose S connected. Then}
\unsure{every invertible Module $\underline{L}$ on X is isomorphic to a Module of the form}

Let us prove 1.1. beginning with uniqueness. First, if S is

we can indeed suppose d = m-n $\hand{\geqslant}$0; if we had d $\hand{>}$0, then $\underline{O}(d)$
would be ample, and could be isomorphic to $\underline{O}_P$ only if P is quasi-affine,
hence finite (since it is proper over k). This already proves uniqueness
of the family $(S_n)_{n\hand{\in}\underline{Z}}$ considered in 1.1. For uniqueness of $\underline{M}$ up to unique

% NOTE: the reviewed source records a long diagonal pen stroke without assigning it cancellation scope over the paragraphs.
Let us prove existence of the $(S_n)$, $\underline{M}$. By the uniqueness already proved,
the question is \uline{local} on S, i.e. we reduce to proving
\uline{Corollary} 1.5. Let $\underline{E}$ be loc free of finite rank on S, P=P($\underline{E}$), $\underline{L}$ an
invertible Module on P, s $\hand{\in}$ S; then there exists an open neighborhood U of s
and an integer n $\hand{\in} \underline{Z}$ such that $\underline{L}\,\hand{|}\,f^{-1}(U)$ is isomorphic to $\underline{O}_P(n)\,\hand{|}\,f^{-1}(U)$.

\hand{\unsure{[|(}}Of course, when the rank of E at s is $\hand{\geq}$ 2, the integer n is
well determined. Moreover 1.5. is trivial when the rank of $\underline{E}$ at s is $\hand{\leq}$ 1\hand{\unsure{]|)}}.
Note that $\underline{E}$ is window dressing, since the question being local, we can already suppose
$\underline{E} = \underline{O}_S^{r+1}$, hence P = $P_S^{r\var{\xout{+1}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_100-v0001}}$\hand{\unsure{]}}. By the patented procedure of par.8, we
further reduce to the case where S is noetherian. We proceed in two steps:

a) S is the spectrum of a field k. We know that $\underline{L}$ is defined
by a graded Module L of finite type over the graded ring k$[t_0,\ldots,t_r]$.
We also know that the restriction \var{\inserted[typed]{$L'$}}{$L'$}{insertion}{ega25_25_100-v0002} of $\overset{\hand{\sim}}{L}$ to punctured affine space
$E_k^{r+1}$ - (0) is precisely the inverse image of $\underline{L}$ by the canonical projection
morphism \var{\inserted[typed]{q:}}{q:}{insertion}{ega25_25_100-v0003} $E_k^{r+1}$ - (0) $\hand{\longrightarrow} P_k^r$, and is therefore an invertible
Module. Let $i : E^{r+1}$-(0)$\hand{\to} E^{r+1}$ be the canonical immersion; it then follows
from the fact that the \var{\inserted[typed]{affine}}{affine}{insertion}{ega25_25_100-v0004} ring k$[t_0,..,t_r]$ of $E^{r+1}$ is factorial, hence a
fortiori its localization at the point 0 of $E^{r+1}$ is factorial, and from the fact
that this last ring is of dimension $\hand{\geq}$ 2, that $i_*(\overset{\hand{\sim}}{L'})$ is an invertible
Module, \var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_100-v0006} hence corresponds to an invertible module \unsure{M|N} over
k$[t_0,..,t_r]$. Moreover M = $\Gamma(E^{r+1}$-0, $\unsure{q'|q^*}(\underline{L}))$ is naturally graded,
finally the homomorphism L $\hand{\to}$ M is evidently an isomorphism
at all the \var{\xout{\illegible{2}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_100-v0007} points of $E^{r+1}$ distinct from 0. Thus, replacing
L by M, we reduce to the case where L is invertible. But
k$[t_0,..,t_r]$ being factorial, \var{\over{L}{L}}{L}{writing over}{ega25_25_100-v0008} is therefore \uline{free} of rank 1, initially
disregarding its grading; but a standard lemma (which is probably
in Bourbaki) implies that it is then free of rank 1
as a graded module, which implies that the associated Module on P\var{\margin{\ensuremath{\backslash}}}{\placedmargin{\ensuremath{\backslash}}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_100-v0009}
\tnote{25-100-1}{Window dressing renders the colloquial de la frime; patented procedure follows procédé bréveté literally. The source has précédons in the sentence translated We proceed in two steps. The canceled uncertain \unsure{e} within factoriel has no English spelling effect. The inserted L-prime, the subsequent tilde, and both candidates in the section formula are retained exactly.}

of Picard, obtained from the section of the latter defined by $\underline{O}_P(1)$, is an
\uline{isomorphism}.

Let P be a projective bundle over a field k. An invertible Module
$\underline{L}$ on P is said to be \uline{of degree} n if $\underline{L}$ is isomorphic to $\underline{O}_P(n)$; when
dim P$\hand{\geq}$1, this determines n in terms of $\underline{L}$, but if dim P $\hand{\leq}$ D
(i.e. p is empty, or reduced to a point) then $\underline{L}$ is degree n for every n.
When P is a projective bundle over an arbitrary base, an invertible
Module $\underline{L}$ on P is said to be of degree n if it is of degree n on every fibr
% NOTE: the end of the preceding source line is cut off at the right edge of the scan.
This determines n, except if all the fibers of P/S are of dim$\hand{\leq}$0, then
$\underline{L}$ is of degree n for every n. To say that $\underline{L}$ is of degree n also means,
by 1.1. and 1.2., that \var{\inserted[typed]{the class}}{the class}{insertion}{ega25_25_102-v0002} \var{\xout{the image}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_102-v0003} of $\underline{L}$ in Pic(P) lies in
the image of \var{\inserted{$\mathrm{Pic}\,S\times\{n\}$ \unsure{by|by}}}{$\mathrm{Pic}\,S\times\{n\}$ \unsure{by|by}}{insertion}{ega25_25_102-v0004} the homomorphism (x) Pic(S)x$\underline{Z}$ $\hand{\longrightarrow}$Pic(P) considered above,
i.e. that $\underline{L}$ is isomorphic to a Module of the form $f^*(\underline{M})\unsure{(|\otimes}n)$, where $\underline{M}$ is
invertible on S. Moreover, when the fibers of P are nonempty
i.e..$\underline{E}$ everywhere of rank $\hand{\geq}$1, then $\underline{M}$ is determined up to unique isomorphism\var{\margin{\ensuremath{/}}}{\placedmargin{\ensuremath{/}}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_102-v0005}
\var{\margin{\textbar}}{\placedmargin{\textbar}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_102-v0006}in terms of $\underline{L}$, as follows again from 1.1. and 1.2. (On this
subject, I realize that 1.1. should have been stated thus, without a hypothesis
on the rank of $\underline{E}$: every invertible $\underline{L}$ on S can be put in the form
indicated in the statement; when the fibers of P are nonempty i.e. the
rank of $\underline{E}$ everywhere $\hand{\neq}$ 0, then $\underline{M}$ is determined up to unique isom by
$\underline{L}$; when the fibers of P are all of dim $\hand{\geq}$1, \var{\inserted{i.e. the rank of $\underline{E}$ everywhere $\geq 2$,}}{i.e. the rank of $\underline{E}$ everywhere $\geq 2$,}{insertion}{ega25_25_102-v0007} then the partition
of S is also uniquely determined by the choice of $\underline{L}$. In this
way, Remark 1. 2. is eliminated and passes into the proof).\var{\margin{\ensuremath{\swarrow}}}{\placedmargin{\ensuremath{\swarrow}}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_102-v0008}

Let P' = P($\underline{E}$') be a second projective bundle; then the determination
of Pic(P) allows us in principle to determine the S-morphisms
g:P$\hand{\to}$P', since these are defined by an invertible Module $\underline{L}$ \var{\inserted{($\simeq g^*\mathcal{O}_{P'}(1)$)}}{($\simeq g^*\mathcal{O}_{P'}(1)$)}{insertion}{ega25_25_102-v0009} on P\var{\margin{\ensuremath{/}}}{\placedmargin{\ensuremath{/}}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_102-v0010}

2. \uline{Relative divisors and invertible sheaves on projective}

\uline{and multiprojective bundles}.

\hand{2.1.} As in no.1, let P=P($\underline{E}$), $\underline{E}$ loc free on S of rank $\hand{\geqslant}$ 2 everywhere.
We propose to determine the set Div(P/S) of relative divisors
\var{\inserted{$\geqslant 0$}}{$\geqslant 0$}{insertion}{ega25_25_106-v0001} on P w.r.t. S. We know that the datum of such a divisor amounts to the
datum of an invertible Module $\underline{L}$ on P, equipped with a transversely regular
section $\hand{\phi}$ of $\underline{L}$. But by 1.1. (disregarding a
possible partition of S, when S is not connected) $\underline{L}$ is isomorphic
to an $\underline{M}\otimes\underline{O}_P(n)$, where $\underline{M}$ is an invertible Module on S, moreover determined
up to unique isomorphism in terms of $\underline{L}$. Moreover, we know
that we then have canonical isoms
\[ \hand{(*)} \qquad f_{\hand{*}}(\underline{L}) \hand{\simeq} \underline{M}\otimes f_{\hand{*}}(\underline{O}_P(\unsure{n|m})) \hand{\simeq} \underline{M}\otimes\underline{Sym}^n(\underline{E}) \]
so the datum of a section \var{\xout{of}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_106-v0002} $\hand{\phi}$ of $\underline{E}$ amounts to the datum of a section
\var{\inserted{$\phi$}}{$\phi$}{insertion}{ega25_25_106-v0003} of $\underline{M}\otimes\underline{Sym}^n$(E). Taking account of the fact that the fibers of P/S are integral,
we moreover see that $\hand{\phi}$ is transversely regular (i.e. regular
on every fiber) iff \hand{$\phi$}(s)$\hand{\neq}$0 for every s$\hand{\in}$S, or equivalently,
i\hand{ff} the homomorphism
\[ \hand{\phi} : \overset{\hand{\vee}}{\underline{M}} \hand{\longrightarrow} \underline{Sym}^n(E) \]
defined by \hand{$\phi$} is ``universally injective'' i.e. loc an isomorphism onto
a direct factor, or equivalently, if its transpose
\[ \hand{\check{\phi}} : \underline{Sym}^n(\underline{E})^{\hand{\vee}} \hand{\longrightarrow} \underline{M} \]
is surjective.

We will say that the relative divisor D on P is \uline{of degree} n
if $\underline{O}_X(\underline{D})= \underline{L}$ is of degree n in the sense of the preceding no. \var{\deleted{Thus, by 1.1.}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_106-v0004}
\var{\deleted{for given D, there exists a unique \var{\inserted[typed]{decomposition}}{decomposition}{insertion}{ega25_25_106-v0006} \var{\xout{partition}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_106-v0007} of S as a sum of opens $S_n$}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_106-v0005}
\var{\deleted{\unsure{(n N)|n N)} such}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_106-v0008}
\tnote{25-106-1}{The abbreviations p. r. à and sss are translated as w.r.t. and iff. In the second iff, the handwritten ff corresponds to the source's handwritten ss. The source says a section of E after the first formula and uses O with subscript X in the degree definition; both are retained.}

When D $\hand{\geq} 0$, this implies $n \hand{\geq} 0$, since if \var{\inserted{\unsure{we had|did not have}}}{\unsure{we had|did not have}}{insertion}{ega25_25_107-v0001} $n \hand{\unsure{<|\leq}} 0$ every section of
$\underline{L}$ on X would be zero. By 1.1., if D is a relative divisor
$\hand{\geq} 0$ on P, then there exists a unique decomposition of D as a disjoint
sum of opens $S_n (n \hand{\in} \underline{N})$ such that for every $n \hand{\in} \underline{N}$, $\underline{L}\hand{|}P\hand{|}S_n$ is of
degree n. This reduces the determination of the set of relative divisors
$\hand{\geq} 0$ to the case of relative divisors $\hand{\geq} 0$ of given degree n. (This
\var{\margin{$/\!/$}}{\placedmargin{$/\!/$}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_107-v0003} \unsure{text|text} will evidently replace the ``disregarding'' above). This said,
the preceding reflections establish

\uline{Proposition} 2.2. Under the preceding hypotheses, we have a one-to-one
correspondence between the set $\mathrm{Div}^{\unsure{n|m}}(\unsure{P|E|R}/S)$ of relative divisors $\hand{\geq} 0$ of
degree n on P, and the set of invertible quotient Modules $\underline{M}$ of
$\underline{\mathrm{Sym}}^{n}(\underline{E})^{\hand{\vee}}$, (or equivalently, the invertible sub-Modules that are loc
direct factors $\overset{\hand{\vee}}{\underline{M}}$ of $\underline{\mathrm{Sym}}^{n}(\underline{E})$). If D and $\underline{M}$ correspond, then
$\underline{O}_P(D)$ is canonically isomorphic to $\underline{M}\otimes\underline{O}_P(n)$, and the section $s_D$ is
identified by this isomorphism with what one \unsure{guesses|becomes}, taking account of $(*)$.

Note that this description is compatible with every base
change in S. Taking account of the interpretation of inv quotient Modules of
$\underline{\mathrm{Sym}}^{n}(\underline{E})^{\hand{\vee}}$ as the sections over S of $P(\underline{\mathrm{Sym}}^{n}(\underline{E})^{\hand{\vee}})$, we find:
\uline{Corollary} 2.3. The subfunctor \var{\deleted{\var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_107-v0005}}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_107-v0004} $\mathrm{Div}^{n}_{P/S}$ of $\mathrm{Div}^{+}_{\unsure{P|E|R}/S}$ is canonically representable
by $P(\underline{\mathrm{Sym}}^{n}(\underline{E})^{\hand{\vee}})$.

Taking account of the considerations of 2.1., it follows:
\uline{Corollary} 2.4. $\underline{\mathrm{Div}}^{+}_{\unsure{P|E|R}/S}$ is canonically representable \var{\xout{between}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_107-v0006} by
the S-pres\unsure{c|b}heme sum of the $P(\underline{\mathrm{Sym}}^{n}_{\underline{P}/S}\unsure{\var{\xout{(}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_107-v0007}|I^{\hand{*}}_{\hand{*}}}\underline{E})^{\hand{\vee}})$, $n \hand{\in} \underline{N}$.
2.5. Suppose now given a finite family $(\underline{E}_i)_{i \hand{\in} I}$ of locally free
Modules \unsure{on|on} S, whence $P_i = P(\underline{E}_i)$ and a P= fiber product of the
$P_i$, also called the \uline{multiprojective bundle} over S defined by $(\underline{E}_i)$. To
simplify the notation, denote by $\underline{O}_i(n)$ the inverse image on P of the

\var{\inserted[typed]{invertible}}{invertible}{insertion}{ega25_25_108-v0001} Module $\underline{O}_{P_i}(n)$ on $P_i$. For every system of integers

This said, 1.1. generalizes as follows:

\uline{Proposition} 2.6. Suppose the $\underline{E}_i$ everywhere of rank $\hand{\geq}$2. Then for every
invertible Module $\underline{L}$ on the multiprojective bundle P, there exists a
\var{\xout{partition}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_108-v0003} decomposition of S as a disjoint sum of opens $\underline{S}_{\underline{n}}$, $\underline{n} \hand{\in} \underline{Z}^I$,

determined, and \var{\xout{the}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_108-v0005} $\underline{M}$ is determined up to unique isomorphism.

\var{\inserted{2.7.}}{2.7.}{insertion}{ega25_25_108-v0006} The proof \var{\xout{follows}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_108-v0007} consists of an immediate reduction to 1.1.
Under the conditions of 2.6., we can therefore associate with every invertible $\underline{L}$
on P a ``multidegree'' $\underline{n} = (\unsure{h|n}_i)_{i \hand{\in} I} \hand{\in} \underline{Z}^{\hand{\unsure{*|x|z}}}(S)^I$, which characterizes $\underline{L}$ up to isomorphism
when Pic(S)=0. We can moreover interpret $n_i$ (called
``the \uline{partial degree} of $\underline{L}$ with respect to the factor $P_i$ of index i''), when
for each i we are given a section $g_i$ of $P_i$\var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_108-v0008} over S (NB such sections
exist in any case locally over S), by noting that this system defines
for every i an S-morphism \var{\xout{$h_i$}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_108-v0009}
\[ h_i : P_i \hand{\longrightarrow} P \quad ; \]
this said, we have
\[ n_i = \deg h_i^{\hand{*}}(\unsure{\underline{L}|\underline{E}}) \quad . \]
One should take care that in general, the $n_i$ are not integers, but locally constant
maps from S to $\underline{Z}$.

Proceeding as in no.1, we can deduce from 2.6. the determination of
morphisms from one \unsure{multiprojective|multiprojective} bundle to another, and in particular that
of automorphisms of a multiprojective bundle. More interesting for us,

in view of par.25 on the \unsure{resultant|resultant} and the discriminant of forms, will be the

If $\underline{D}$ is a relative divisor on P, we define its multidegree as being
% NOTE: the right edge of the source page cuts off the final letters of "étan[t]" and "ramené[e]".
that of $\underline{O}_P(D)$. As above, the determination of $\mathrm{Div}^{+}(P/S)$ reduces
to that of $\mathrm{Div}^{\underline{n}}(P/S)$, for a given multidegree $\underline{n}\hand{\in}\underline{\unsure{N|M}}^{I}$, which provides an
isomorphism
\[ \underline{L} =\underline{O}_X(D) \hand{\simeq} \underline{M} \otimes_{\underline{O}_S} \underline{O}_P(\underline{n}) \ . \]
But by Chap II par.2 we obtain (\var{\xout{or by Künneth}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_109-v0003}
\[ (xx) \qquad f_{\hand{*}}(\underline{D}) = \underline{M} \otimes f_{\hand{*}}(\underline{O}_P(\underline{n})) = \underline{M} \otimes \hand{\bigotimes}_i \underline{\mathrm{Sym}}^{n_i}(\underline{E}_i) \quad . \]
Proceeding now as for 2.2. we find

\uline{Proposition} 2.9. With the preceding notation, to be recalled, we have\var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_109-v0004} a
can one-to-one corr between the set $\mathrm{Div}^{\underline{n}}(P/S)$ of relative divisors of
multidegree $\underline{n}$ on P, and the set of invertible quotient Modules $\underline{M}$
of $\hand{\bigotimes}_i \underline{\mathrm{Sym}}^{n_i}(\underline{E}_i)^{\hand{\vee}}$ (or equivalently ...). If D and $\underline{M}$ correspond,
$\underline{O}_P(D)$ is can isomorphic to $\underline{M}\otimes\underline{O}_P(\underline{n})$, and $s_D$ is then identified
with what one guesses, taking account of (xx).

\uline{Corollary} 2.10. The subfunctor $\mathrm{Div}^{\underline{n}}_{P/S}$ of $\mathrm{Div}^{+}_{P/S}$ corresponding to
relative divisors of multidegree $\underline{n}$ is can representable by the projective
bundle $P(\hand{\bigotimes}_i \underline{\mathrm{Sym}}^{n_i}(\underline{E}_i)^{\hand{\vee}})$, and $\underline{\mathrm{Div}}^{+}_{P/S}$ is can repr by the prescheme
sum of these \unsure{latter|latter}, for $\underline{n}\hand{\in}\underline{N}^{I}$.

2.11. The preceding very simple determination of the $\mathrm{Div}_{P/S}$ is due to the
very simple structure of Pic(P/S) (in fact, to the ``discrete'' structure of the
Picard prescheme $\underline{\mathrm{Pic}}_{P/S}$ ....). We can abstract the reasoning
carried out, which amounts essentially to establishing a ``relative'' representability
(with respect to $\underline{\mathrm{Pic}}$). F$_o$r this, let us be given a morphism
\[ f\colon X \hand{\to} S \]
proper and flat of finite presentation, \uline{and} an invertible Module $\underline{L}$ on X.

formed by the positive relative divisors such that $\underline{O}_X$(D) is isomorphic to
a Module of the form $\underline{L}\otimes_{\underline{O}_X}\underline{M}$, where $\underline{M}$ is an inv Module on S (depending on
D). We will suppose that we have
\[ f_{\hand{*}}(\underline{O}_X)\overset{\hand{\sim}}{\hand{\longleftarrow}}\underline{O}_S \quad , \]
which implies that above $\underline{M}$ is determined up to unique isom in terms
of D, as
\[ \underline{M}\hand{\simeq} f_{\hand{*}}(\underline{L}^{-1}\otimes\underline{O}_X(D)) \quad . \]
The datum of a D corresponding to a given $\underline{M}$ therefore amounts to the datum
\var{\inserted[typed]{\var{\xout{\unsure{$\underline{\phi}$|ø}\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_110-v0002}}}{\var{\xout{\unsure{$\underline{\phi}$|ø}\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_110-v0002}}{insertion}{ega25_25_110-v0001}
of a section\var{\xout{s}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_110-v0003} $\hand{\phi}$ of $\underline{L}\otimes\underline{M}$ that is transversely regular. But we saw in
Chap III par 7 \var{\xout{\unsure{f$_*$}($\underline{L}\otimes\underline{M}$)\illegible{1}\unsure{f$_*$}($\underline{L}$)$\otimes$M\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_110-v0004} that there \var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_110-v0005} exists a Module Q of
finite presentation on S, whose formation moreover commutes with every
base change, and an isomorphism of functors in \unsure{$\underline{N}$|$\underline{G}$} (a varying qu coh
Module on S)
\[ f_{\hand{*}}(\underline{L}\otimes\underline{G})\hand{\simeq} \mathrm{Hom}(\underline{Q},G) \quad . \]
(In truth, in loc cit we supposed S loc noetherian, but we
evidently dispense with this hypothesis by the patented procedure,
taking account of the commutation of Q with base\var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_110-v0007} change). In particular,
the datum of $\hand{\phi}$ is equivalent to \var{\xout{\unsure{a}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_110-v0008} the datum of a homomorphism
\[ \hand{\psi} : Q \hand{\longrightarrow} M \ . \]
A necessary condition for $\hand{\phi}$ to be transversely regular, which
is sufficient when the fibers of X are integral, is that $\hand{\phi}$ be
$\hand{\neq} 0$ \var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_110-v0009} fiber by fiber, which in terms of $\hand{\psi}$ simply means that
$\hand{\psi}$ is surjective, hence that \var{\xout{M\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_110-v0010} $\hand{\psi}$ corresponds to a section of the projective
bundle $\underline{P}(\underline{Q})$ over S. O$\unsure{\overset{\illegible{1}}{n}_{\unsure{n|\sim}}|n}$e thus obtains

\uline{Proposition} 2.1\unsure{\var{\over{1}{2}}{2}{writing over}{ega25_25_110-v0011}|1}. \var{\inserted[typed]{With the preceding notation}}{With the preceding notation}{insertion}{ega25_25_110-v0012} \var{\xout{Under the preceding conditions}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_110-v0013},\var{\xout{on X/S}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_110-v0014} Div$^{\mathrm{L}}$(X/S) is

\tnote{25-110-1}{Subgroup translates the literal sous-groupe; the formula with tensor product over O-subscript-X is retained. Qu coh abbreviates quasi-coherent. the section $\hand{\phi}$ of $\underline{L}\otimes\underline{M}$ defined by $\hand{\psi}$: $Q\hand{\longrightarrow}\underline{M}$ is transversely
regular.

Suppose now that the hypothesis $\underline{O}_S\overset{\hand{\sim}}{\hand{\longrightarrow}}f_{\hand{*}}(\underline{O}_X)$ is still true
after every base change, or equivalently by III 7,
that we have the condition
(xxx) \qquad\qquad $k(s)\overset{\hand{\sim}}{\hand{\longrightarrow}}H^o(X_s,\underline{O}_{X_s})$
for every $s\hand{\in} S$. Then 2.12. also applies to every $X_{S'}/S'$, for an
arbitrary base change $S'\hand{\rightarrow} S$. We thus obtain
\uline{Theorem} 2.13. Let $f\colon X\hand{\longrightarrow} S$ be a \var{\deleted{flat}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_111-v0001} morphism of finite presentation,
proper and flat satisfying (xxx) above, $\underline{L}$ an invertible Module
on $X$; consider the subfunctor $\mathrm{Div}^{L}_{X/S}$ of $\mathrm{Div}^{+}_{X/S}$ defined above in
terms of $\underline{L}$. \var{\xout{This functor}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_111-v0002} There exists a Module of finite presentation $\underline{Q}$ on
$S$ such that the preceding functor is representable by a retrocompact open
subprescheme of the projective bundle $\underline{P}(\underline{\unsure{Q|A}})$; when the fibers of $X/S$
are geometrically integral, then $\mathrm{Div}^{L}_{X/S}$ is representable by this
projective \var{\inserted[typed]{bundle}}{bundle}{insertion}{ega25_25_111-v0003} \var{\xout{scheme}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_111-v0004} itself.

The last assertion follows immediately from what we had said
before. F$\unsure{\underset{\cap}{o}|o}$r the general case, we had already noted that we have a \unsure{monomorphism}
\[
\mathrm{Div}^{L}_{X/S}\hand{\longrightarrow}\underline{P}(\underline{Q}) \quad ,
\]
we reduce to proving that the latter is representable by a quasi-compact open
immersion, which reduces us to proving that if we are given
a section of $P(\underline{\unsure{Q|A}})$ over $S$ i.e. an invertible quotient Module $\underline{M}$ of $\underline{Q}$,
whence a section $\hand{\phi}$ of $\underline{L}\otimes\underline{M}$ nonzero on every fiber, then the \var{\inserted[typed]{sub}}{sub}{insertion}{ega25_25_111-v0005}functor
$\unsure{\overline{U}|U}$ of the final functor $S$ on $(\mathrm{Sch})_{/S}$ ``consisting in making $\hand{\phi}$ transversely
regular'' is representable by a retrocompact open of $S$. But
the fact that it is representable by an open follows from the fact that $f$ is
proper and that transverse regularity is an open condition (cf par.
11 ...), retrocompactness follows immediately by reduction to the
noetherian case.
\tnote{25-111-1}{The superscript letter o in the cohomology expression remains as written. The uncertain marked o within Pour is retained in For. The final-functor terminology follows the supplied glossary, and all projective-bundle letters, including Q or A, keep their source alternatives.}

One can also note in a remark that when X and T are both
flat loc of finite presentation over S, with fibers $(S_1\unsure{)|r}$ and geom irred.,
the symmetry $D \hand{\rightsquigarrow} {}^{t}D$ gives a bijection between
families of divisors of X/S parametrized by T which are without fixed points
and families of divisors of T/S parametrized by X which are without fixed
points. To \unsure{dispense} in this statement with the specific hypotheses
made on the fibers of X/S and T/S , one should replace
``fixed points'' by ``fixed points in the broad sense'', meaning by
a fixed point in the\var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_114-v0001} broad sense of D an $x \hand{\in} X$ such that D is not a
relative \var{\deleted{Cartier}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_114-v0002} divisor \var{\xout{at}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_114-v0003} \var{\inserted[typed]{with respect to X at all}}{with respect to X at all}{insertion}{ega25_25_114-v0004} the points of $\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(x)$ . If W is the open set of
points of $X\times_S T$ at which D is \var{\xout{not}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_114-v0006} a relative \var{\deleted{Cartier}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_114-v0007} divisor with
respect to X, the set of fixed points of D in the broad sense is
\var{\xout{\unsure{example|the example}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_114-v0008} equal to $\mathrm{pr}_1(X\times_S T - W)$; when $T \hand{\to} S$ is proper, it is therefore
a closed subset Z' of X, \var{\xout{and one obtains}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_114-v0009} In any case, one obtains a
family of divisors of T/S parametrized by $X-\overset{\hand{\relbar}}{Z'}$ . The hypothesis that the
fibers of T/S are $(S_1)$ and geom irreducible \var{\xout{ensures}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_114-v0010} \var{\inserted[typed]{serves}}{serves}{insertion}{ega25_25_114-v0011} precisely to
ensure that $Z=Z'$ (fixed points $\hand{\unsure{=|\ne}}$ fixed points in the broad sense). Geometrically,
assuming for simplicity that S=Spec(k), k an algebraically closed field

such that $x \hand{\in} D_t$ for every $t \hand{\in} T'(k)$).

$\underline{J}\hand{\to}\underline{O}_X$ is indeed reconstructed by applying the functor $i_{\hand{\unsure{*|\relbar}}}$ to
$\underline{J}\,\hand{|}\,X-Z" \hand{\unsure{\longrightarrow|\relbar}} \underline{O}_X\,\hand{|}\,X-Z"$ . Now since $\underline{J}$ is invertible, it is flat over S \var{\over{and}{\unsure{and}}}{\unsure{and}}{writing over}{ega25_25_118-v0004}
\var{\xout{fibers of}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_118-v0005} $x\hand{\in} Z" \hand{\Rightarrow} \mathrm{prof}_x\,\underline{J}_{s\,\hand{\unsure{*|x}}} \hand{\geqslant} 2$. It therefore suffices to prove the
\uline{Lemma} \hand{3.2}. Let $X\hand{\to} S$ be loc of finite presentation, F a Module of finite
presentation on X flat rel to S, T a closed subset of X; suppose that for
\var{\margin{cf\ \S 20.11}}{\placedmargin{cf\ \S 20.11}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_118-v0006}
every $x\hand{\in} X$ over $s\hand{\in} S$, one has \hand{\unsure{/}} $\mathrm{prof}_x F_{s\,\var{\xout{\unsure{n|x}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_118-v0007}}\hand{\geqslant} 1$ (resp. $\mathrm{prof}_x F_s \hand{\geqslant} 2$).
Then the canonical homomorphism $F\hand{\to} i_{\hand{*}}(F\hand{|}X-T)$ is injective (resp.
bijective), where $i:X-T\hand{\to} T$ is the canonical immersion.

Proof of the lemma: one can suppose S,X affine, and
reduce by the patented procedure to the case of noetherian S. Then the hypothesis
implies, by virtue of par.6 , that $\mathrm{prof}_x F \hand{\geqslant} \mathrm{prof}_x F_s$ for every .
$x\hand{\in} X$ over $s\hand{\in} S$, hence $\mathrm{prof}_x F_s \hand{\geqslant} 1$ (resp.$\hand{\geqslant} 2$) if $x\hand{\in} T$. One then concludes
by par.5 . (NB To do things properly, this lemma should appear in par.
11 under the heading; elimination of noetherian hypotheses ...).

It remains finally to check the last assertion of prop.2, namely
that \var{\deleted{\unsure{Z}}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_118-v0010}\var{\inserted[typed]{X-Z}}{X-Z}{insertion}{ega25_25_118-v0011} is exactly the \unsure{domain} of definition of the rational
map rel to S defined by f. Let $U\hand{\supset} X-Z$ be this domain; it then follows from
proposition 1 that $U\hand{\longrightarrow} P$ is associated with a\var{\xout{\unsure{family}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_118-v0013}\var{\inserted[typed]{lin. system}}{ lin. system}{insertion}{ega25_25_118-v0014} of divisors
D' on U\unsure{/|x}S parametrized by $\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$ , and one has $D'\hand{|}(X-Z)\times_S\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P} = D\hand{|}(X-Z)\times_S\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$ . Applying
the uniqueness result \hand{(}already proved\hand{)} to D' and $D\hand{|}U\times_S\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$ , one therefore sees
that these last two divisors are equal, so $D\hand{|}U\times_S\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$ has no
fixed points, i.e. $Z\hand{\cap} U=\hand{\emptyset}$, hence U=X-Z , QED.

\var{\over{7}{4}}{4}{writing over}{ega25_25_123-v0001}. \uline{Linear systems of divisors and invertible Modules}.

Using the result of no.1, we shall give a complete description
of linear systems on X in terms of invertible sheaves
on X. \var{\inserted{We can obviously suppose $\check{P}\to S$ surjective. Then $X\times_S\check{P}\to \check{P}$ being so\unsure{,|.}}}{We can obviously suppose $\check{P}\to S$ surjective. Then $X\times_S\check{P}\to \check{P}$ being so\unsure{,|.}}{insertion}{ega25_25_123-v0002} \var{\deleted{Indeed,}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_123-v0003}\hand{and,} by the generalities of \var{\over{no.2}{\S 20.3}}{\S 20.3}{writing over}{ega25_25_123-v0004}, giving a
\var{\deleted{Cartier}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_123-v0005} divisor D on $X\times_S\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$ \var{\xout{(projective bundle over X)}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_123-v0006} amounts to
giving an invertible Module $\underline{N}$ on $X\times_S\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$ , and a regular section
$\hand{\phi}$ of the latter. \var{\xout{\unsure{By vir}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_123-v0007} The hypothesis that D is a linear system of
divisors on X parametrized by $\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$ is then expressed by the two conditions
1º) the $\hand{\phi}_t$ ($t\hand{\in}\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$) induced by $\hand{\phi}$ on the fibers of $Xs_S\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$ over $\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$
are regular (which implies that $\hand{\phi}$ is regular), and 2º) the $\underline{N}_x$ ($x\hand{\in} X$)
induced by $\underline{N}$ \var{\xout{are}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_123-v0009} on the fibers of $X\times_S\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$ over X are \uline{of degree} 1 .
Now giving an invertible $\underline{\unsure{N|E}}$ on \unsure{the} projective bundle $X\times_S\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$ over X,
satisfying condition 2º) above, is equivalent by no.1
to giving an invertible Module $\underline{L}$ on X, $\underline{N}$ being determined in terms
of $\underline{L}$ by
\[ \underline{N}\hand{\simeq}\underline{L}\otimes_{\underline{O}_{\unsure{S|X}}}\underline{O}_{\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}}(1) \quad , \]
and $\underline{L}$ being moreover determined in terms of $\underline{N}$ by $\underline{L}\hand{\unsure{\simeq|\longrightarrow}} pr_{1\hand{*}}(\underline{N}(-1))$,
where (-1) denotes \var{\inserted{\unsure{the}}}{\unsure{the}}{insertion}{ega25_25_123-v0010} tensoring with $\underline{O}_{\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}}(-1)$ over $\underline{O}_S$ . Giving $\hand{\phi}$
amounts to giving a section of $\underline{L}\otimes_{\underline{O}_S}\underline{O}_{\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}}(1)$ , i.e. a section
\var{\margin{$\underline{O}_{X\times_S\check{P}}(1)$}}{\placedmargin{$\underline{O}_{X\times_S\check{P}}(1)$}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_123-v0011}
of $pr_{1\hand{*}}(\underline{L}\otimes_{\underline{O}_X}\underline{O}_{\var{\over{P}{\unsure{X\times_S\check{P}}}}{\unsure{X\times_S\check{P}}}{writing over}{ega25_25_123-v0012}}(1))$ = $\underline{L}\otimes_{\underline{O}_S}\unsure{\var{\over{pr}{\illegible{1}}}{\illegible{1}}{writing over}{ega25_25_123-v0013}|pr}_{\hand{*}}(\underline{O}_{\unsure{\var{\over{X\times_S P}{\check{P}}}{\check{P}}{writing over}{ega25_25_123-v0014}}}(1))$, \var{\deleted{\var{\xout{$\unsure{=}\underline{L}\otimes_{\underline{O}_S}\overset{\hand{\unsure{\vee}}}{\underline{E}}$ i.e. a homomorphism}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_123-v0016}}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_123-v0015}
\var{\deleted{\var{\xout{$\underline{\unsure{E|R}}$ $\underline{E}$ \illegible{1} $\otimes$}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_123-v0018}}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_123-v0017} now by III 2 one has $\unsure{\var{\over{pr}{\illegible{1}}}{\illegible{1}}{writing over}{ega25_25_123-v0019}|pr}_{\hand{*}}(\underline{O}_{X\times_S\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}}(1))\hand{\simeq}\overset{\hand{\vee}}{\underline{E}}_X$ , hence
giving $\hand{\phi}$ is equivalent to \var{\xout{a h}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_123-v0020} giving a homomorphism $g^{\hand{*}}(\underline{E})\hand{\to}\underline{L}$,
or equivalently, a morphism \var{\inserted[typed]{u:}}{u:}{insertion}{ega25_25_123-v0021} $\underline{E}\hand{\to} g_{\hand{*}}(\underline{L})$ (NB $g:X\hand{\to} S$ is
the canonical projection). It remains to express condition 1º) above
in terms of u. Since the constructions made commute with
base change, it suffices to express this condition fiber by fiber\hand{,}
and taking into account that the points of $\overset{\hand{\vee}}{P}$ with values in an extension k of
k(s) correspond exactly to the lines in $E(s)\otimes_{k(s)}k$, this

\uline{Proposition} \var{\over{5}{4}}{4}{writing over}{ega25_25_124-v0002}.1. Le\hand{t} $g:X\hand{\to} S$ be a flat morphism loc of finite

the corresponding section u(t) of $\underline{L}_{s\,k}$ on $X_{s\,k}$ is regular.

One will note that when the fibers of X are \var{\xout{($S_1$) and geom irred}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_124-v0008}

\[ \mathrm{Hom}\,(Q,F) \hand{\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }} g_{\hand{*}}(\underline{L}\otimes_{\underline{O}_S}F) \quad . \]

by $\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{P}$ , and associated with $\underline{L}$ (in the sense of \hand{4}.1.) correspond bijectively

The existence of $Q$ is reduced by the patented procedure to the case of noetherian S,
and in that case is precisely III 7.7.6. (the hypothesis on the
fibers of X being moreover \unsure{unnecessary}).\tnote{25-125-1}{The French word ends in an uncertain e or è; the lexical reading is ``inutile''. The uncertainty remains marked in the translation.}
Since $\underline{E}$ is loc free of finite type,
giving a hom $\underline{E}\hand{\longrightarrow} f(\underline{L})$ is equivalent to giving a section of
$\underline{L}\otimes_{\underline{O}_S}\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{\underline{E}}$ , hence to giving a homomorphism $Q\hand{\longrightarrow}\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{\underline{E}}$ . It remains to express
that the condition considered in \hand{4}.1. is indeed satisfied, which (thanks to
the hypothesis made on the fibers of X/S) reduces to checking that
fiber by fiber the corresponding homomorphism $E(s)\hand{\longrightarrow}$ \var{\xout{Q(s)}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_125-v0007}\hand{$\vee$}
$H^0(X_s,L_s)\simeq\mathrm{Hom}_{k(s)}(Q(s),k(s))$ is injective, or again that $Q(s)\hand{\longrightarrow}\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{E}(s)$ is surjective,
which by Nakayama also means that $Q$ \quad $E$ is surjective. The ``modulo
sections of $\underline{O}_S$ '' comes from the ``modulo isomorphism'' in \hand{4}.1.\hand{/}

One can \var{\xout{xxxxxxxxx}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_125-v0008}\var{\inserted[typed]{interpret}}{interpret}{insertion}{ega25_25_125-v0009} \hand{4}.1. by another route, using the fact
that $P(\underline{Q})$ represents the \var{\xout{xxxxxxxx}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_125-v0010} subfunctor of $\mathrm{Div}_{X/S}$ defined by
$\underline{L}$, by virtue of n$^{\circ}$2. Consequently, a linear system of divisors parametr
by $\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{P}$ \var{\inserted[typed]{and associated with $\underline{L}$}}{and associated with $\underline{L}$}{insertion}{ega25_25_125-v0012} is interpreted as a morphism $\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{P} = P(\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{\underline{E}})\hand{\longrightarrow} P(Q)$; the
\uline{linear} character of the family of divisors defined by such a morphism
is then interpreted by the fact that this morphism is ``linear'', i.e.
precisely defined by a surjective morphism $Q\hand{\longrightarrow}\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{\underline{E}}$ . \var{\margin{$\ulcorner$}}{\placedmargin{$\ulcorner$}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_125-v0013} One also sees
in\var{\xout{xx}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_125-v0014} this case that the morphism $\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{P}\hand{\longrightarrow}\mathrm{Div}_{X/S}$ is a monomorphism \var{\deleted{\illegible{2}}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_125-v0015}
(since $\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{P}\hand{\longrightarrow} P(Q)\hand{\hookrightarrow}\mathrm{Div}_{X/S}$ is one), a \var{\inserted{more}}{more}{insertion}{ega25_25_125-v0016} general fact moreover, cf. the corollary
below. Let us \var{\inserted[typed]{then}}{then}{insertion}{ega25_25_125-v0017} agree to say that \unsure{two} linear families of divisors
of X/S, parametrized by the projective bundles $\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{P},\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{P}'$, are \uline{isomorphic}
when they are transformed into each other by an S-isomorphism $\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{P}\hand{\longrightarrow}\overset{\hand{\scriptscriptstyle\vee}}{P}'$ ,
(which will moreover be unique thanks to the fact that there are monomorphisms
into $\mathrm{Div}_{X/S}$ ). \var{\deleted{We shall call a linear system of divisors in X/S}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_125-v0018}
(\var{\deleted{without reference to a specified projective bundle parametrizing it) a}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_125-v0019}
\tnote{25-125-2}{In the French word translated as ``two'', the second letter is uncertain between e and a. The clipped ``paramétr'' earlier in the paragraph is retained as the fragment ``parametr''. of a); on the other hand, b) holds under less restrictive
hypotheses than a). Care must be taken that a) becomes false when one abandons

canonical immersion of X into $P^1_k$ . Then the two \var{\xout{morphisms}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_127-v0005} points a and b
define the same divisors of X (namely the zero divisor), without being
identical themselves.

Dear Dieudonné,

Thank you for your letter of the 24\textsuperscript{th} and for the table of contents of sections
16 to 19. I would be glad to receive, when you have an opportunity, the provisional table
of contents of sections 20 and 21; I agree to include them in
fascicle 4 of Chap IV. But how do you want to subdivide \var{\xout{them}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_134-v0003}\var{\inserted[typed]{my old section 20}}{ my old section 20}{insertion}{ega25_25_134-v0004}, and
what will the titles of the two parts be \unsure{?|2} Since I am beginning to
lose track of the plan, and it is sometimes convenient to \unsure{be able to} refer
to a section no. without screwing up too much, I give you here what
seems to me to be the current plan; tell me whether you agree:

20. ???

21. ???

22. Linear systems, complements on the Picard group.

23. Grassmannians.

24. Smooth forms, ordinary quadratic singularities.

25. Hyperplane sections and all that crap.

26. Resultant and discriminant.

27. Infinitesimal extensions.

Section 25, \unsure{incidentally}, may well be very long, and I can already see you
wanting to subdivide it into \unsure{two}! Yet $27=3^{\hand{3}}$ is such a pretty
number!

There is no question of my publishing the former Appendix to section 18
under my name; your exposition has almost nothing left in common with
the vague handwritten notes I had given you, if indeed I ever
gave you any, and did not merely say to you: you only have to do

The source also has the spellings paffois, Systêmes, manuscriptes, and j-amais; these have not been imitated with invented English misspellings. The informal wording ``without screwing up too much'' and ``all that crap'' renders sans trop déconner and bordel.}

\RegisterPage{ega25_25_137}{%
% Nouveau EGA V (cote 25): archive cote 25, site page 137 (PDF page 138).
% English translation of the checked French annotated master.
% AI-translated by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode).
\scanpage{25/137}
\mspage{\hand{40}}

IV 21 Invertible sheaves and relative divisors on projective
and multiprojective bundles; linear systems of divisors.

1. Invertible sheaves on a projective bundle; application to
morphisms from one projective bundle to another.

2. Representability of $\underline{\mathrm{Div}}^{L}_{X/S}$; \var{\inserted[typed]{relative}}{relative}{insertion}{ega25_25_137-v0002} divisors on projective and
multiprojective bundles.

3. Linear systems of divisors$_{\mathrm{x}}$ and morphisms into projective
bundles.

4. Linear systems of divisors$_{\mathrm{x}}$ and invertible Modules.

The results developed in this section and the following ones
are already partly global in nature and give, in particular, further
results on projective schemes, using \var{\xout{in an essential way}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_137-v0003} the
global constructions of Chap II, and even here certain results of
Chap III, in addition to the purely local results of this Chapter IV.

One of the aims of this section is to develop the language of
``linear systems of divisors'', linked on the one hand to the classification of
morphisms into a projective bundle, and on the other to that of invertible Modules
on a given relative prescheme. Let us observe here that the
truly natural ``parameter schemes'' for linear systems of
divisors are the \uline{Brauer-Séveri} schemes, which generalize projective
bundles and can be defined, for example, as bundles that become
isomorphic to a projective bundle after a surjective étale extension of
the base. Since their study uses descent theory, developed
in Chap V, and since moreover their classification is equivalent to that of
\var{\xout{\unsure{principal homogeneous bundles}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_137-v0005} torsors with group the projective group, we
refer to Chap VI$_{\mathrm{x}}$ of our learned work for the study of these schemes and their links with the notion of a
linear system of divisors.

\mspage{\hand{137}}
\tnote{25-137-1}{The canceled fragments lesxf and fibr have no separate English lexical content and are recorded as omitted French-only cancellations. The source spellings systêmes and desur, and the split inver/sibles, have not been imitated with English spelling errors. The lowered x characters following divisors and VI remain exactly as in the French master.}

\RegisterPage{ega25_25_140}{%
% Nouveau EGA V (cote 25): archive cote 25, site page 140 (PDF page 141).

IV 16

A new n$^{\text{o}}$: \uline{Singular and supersingular set of a function},
\uline{and differential criteria}.

This n$^{\text{o}}$ will be used in section 20 on hyperplane sections, but its
natural place seems to me to be in section 16.

\uline{Definition} 1 Let X be a regular prescheme, $\hand{\phi}$ a section of $\underline{O}_X$. A
point $x \hand{\in} X$ is called a \uline{singular} \var{\xout{\illegible{3}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_140-v0002} \uline{zero} for $\hand{\phi}$
if we have $\hand{\phi}_x \hand{\in} \underline{m}_x^2$, a \uline{supersingular} zero if it is a singular zero
and if in addition the element of $\underline{m}_x^2/\underline{m}_x^3 \hand{\simeq} \mathrm{Sym}(\underline{m}_x/\underline{m}_x^2)$ that it defines,
interpreted as a quadratic form on the dual $\underline{t}_x$ of $\underline{m}_x/\underline{m}_x^2$ over k(x),
is a \var{\deleted{non-}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_140-v0003}degenerate form. (A singular zero that is not supersingular
is sometimes called an \uline{ordinary singular zero}).

\uline{Remarks} 2 If $x \hand{\in} V(\hand{\phi})$\hand{,} then x is a \var{\inserted[typed]{non-}}{non-}{insertion}{ega25_25_140-v0004}singular zero of $\hand{\phi}$ iff
$\hand{\phi}_x \hand{\neq} 0$ and x is a nonsingular, i.e. regular, point of $V(\hand{\phi})$,
i.e. iff x is a regular point of $V(\hand{\phi})$ and $V(\hand{\phi}) \hand{\neq} X$ in a neighborhood of
x. \var{\deleted{One can prove that if x is singular for $\hand{\phi}$, it is ordinary
singular iff $\hand{\phi}_x \hand{\neq} 0$ and the multiplicity of $\underline{O}_{V(\hand{\phi}),x}$ is equal to 2
(or, as one also sometimes says, x is an \uline{ordinary singular point}
\uline{of the prescheme} $V(\hand{\phi})$); thus an $x \hand{\in} V(\hand{\phi})$ is not supersingular \var{\inserted[typed]{for $\hand{\phi}$}}{for $\hand{\phi}$}{insertion}{ega25_25_140-v0007} iff
$\hand{\phi}_x \hand{\neq} 0$ and the multiplicity of $O_{V(\hand{\phi}),x}$ is $\hand{\leq} 2$.}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_140-v0006}

\uline{Definition} 3. Let X be a prescheme smooth over a field k, $\hand{\phi}$ a
section of $\underline{O}_X$, $x \hand{\in} V(\hand{\phi})$. We say that x is a \uline{geometrically}
\uline{singular} (resp. \uline{geometrically \unsure{supersingular}}) zero of $\hand{\phi}$ relative to k,
if for every extension k' of k and every point \hand{$\xi$} of X with values in
k\hand{,} localized at x, the \var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_140-v0009} corresponding point x' of $X_{k'}$ is a
\var{\xout{\unsure{geom}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_140-v0010} singular (resp. supersingular) zero of $\hand{\phi}_{k'}$.

\uline{Proposition} 7. Under the preceding conditions (to be recalled), the underlying
set of $V(\hand{\phi})^{\text{sup sing}}$ is precisely the set of points of

over S of relative dimensions m-1 and m respectively) is \uline{ramified}.

In papa's terms (which should be pointed out in a remark), a point
$x \hand{\in} V(\hand{\phi})$ is therefore supersingular relative to Y iff ``it consists of at
least two coincident singular points'' ....

One can and should make Prop. 7 more precise from the point of view \var{\inserted[typed]{of an identity of}}{of an identity of}{insertion}{ega25_25_145-v0002} \var{\xout{of the}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_145-v0003} subpreschemes,

defined as a closed subprescheme of X, and one can also define
a natural closed subprescheme of $V^1$ in such a way that its underlying
set is the set of ramification points relative to Y.
Indeed, one must express the set of points where a certain homomorphism
of loc free modules $Q$ ( $=\underline{\hand{\Omega}}^1_{Y/S}\otimes\underline{O}_{V^1}$ ) $\hand{\longrightarrow}$ $R$ ( $=\underline{\hand{\Omega}}^1_{V^1/S}$ )

also the set of zeros of the evident section of \uline{Hom} ( $\hand{\bigwedge}^{m} Q$, $\hand{\bigwedge}^{m} M$)
$\hand{\simeq} (\hand{\bigwedge}^{q-r} Q)\otimes(\hand{\bigwedge}^{r} R^{\hand{\illegible{1}}})$$\otimes(\hand{\bigwedge}^{q} Q)$\hand{$^{\vee}$}, hence the underlying set of the closed \var{\inserted[typed]{sub}}{sub}{insertion}{ega25_25_145-v0004}prescheme
of zeros of this section, namely \uline{Ram}($V^1/Y$). I claim that this latter
subscheme is identical to $V(\hand{\phi})^{\text{sup sing}}$. This is a simple exercise
on the diagram above, taking into account that $V(\hand{\phi})^{\text{sup sing}}$ is defined
by the same procedure as that given for $Q\hand{\longrightarrow} R$, but in terms of
the homomorphism $P$ ( $= \overset{\hand{\vee}}{\underline{P}}{}^1_{X/Y}\otimes\underline{O}_{V^1}$ ) $\hand{\longrightarrow}$ $S$ ($=\underline{\hand{\Omega}}^1_{X/Y}\otimes\underline{O}_{V^1}$), as
follows from the description of \hand{$\mu$} given above. We are then
reduced to the following general situation:

Having reached this admirable degree of generality, I unfortunately
realize that these developments are still too particular, and that instead
of a subprescheme defined by a single section of $\underline{O}_X$, one should
consider the one defined by m sections, or, what\hand{/}amounts to the same thing, by a
homomorphism $\underline{E} \hand{\longrightarrow} \underline{O}_X$, where $\underline{E}$ is a loc free Module of rank m. I
leave it to you to decide whether to begin from the outset with the
general case, following the principle that one must proceed from the general to the
particular.

Let us first introduce terminology for rings A with
augmentation $A \hand{\to} A/I$ (which will also be used in the sheaf
context). The augmentation is called \uline{regular} (or should we say
quasi-regular, with the definitions adopted in section 19?) if \var{\inserted[typed]{a)}}{a)}{insertion}{ega25_25_149-v0002} $I/I^2$ is
a projective A/I-Module of finite type, and \var{\inserted[typed]{b)}}{b)}{insertion}{ega25_25_149-v0003} the homomorphism
\[ \theta\colon \mathrm{Sym}\,(I/I^2) \hand{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{gr}_I(A) \]
is an isomorphism. We shall say that the augmentation is \var{\inserted{of type}}{of type}{insertion}{ega25_25_149-v0004} ``\uline{ordinary}
\uline{quadratic}'' when a) above holds, as well as b') the preceding canonical
homomorphism has a kernel generated by $\theta^2$, which kernel $\underline{K}$
is a ``nondegenerate'' invertible \var{\inserted[typed]{sub-}}{sub-}{insertion}{ega25_25_149-v0005}Module of $\mathrm{Sym}^2(I/I^2)$. By ``nondegenerate''
we mean that the corresponding homomorphism
\[ \underline{K} \otimes (\underline{I}/\underline{I}^2)^{\hand{\vee}} \hand{\longrightarrow} \underline{I}/\underline{I}^2 \]\var{\margin{\unsure{$\prime$}}}{\placedmargin{\unsure{$\prime$}}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_149-v0006}
(obtained using the canonical homomorphism
\[ \mathrm{Sym}^2(I/I^2) \hand{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{Hom}\ (\ (I/I^2)^{\hand{\vee}}\ ,\ I/I^2\ )\quad ) \]
is bijective, or equivalently surjective (since these are
projective Modules \var{\inserted[typed]{over A/I}}{over A/I}{insertion}{ega25_25_149-v0007} of the same rank at every point), or again: taking
locally a basis \var{\inserted{$\phi$}}{$\phi$}{insertion}{ega25_25_149-v0008} of $\underline{K}$, \var{\xout{the corresponding homomorphism}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_149-v0009} the corresponding
quadratic form on $(I/I^2)^{\hand{\vee}}$ is nondegenerate. It suffices

moreover to verify these latter conditions \var{\xout{xx}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_150-v0002}\var{\inserted[typed]{for}}{for}{insertion}{ega25_25_150-v0003} the reduced fibers
at the various prime (or even only maximal) ideals of A/I.
\uline{Proposition} 8. For the augmentation A$\hand{\rightarrow}$A/I to be \var{\inserted{of type}}{of type}{insertion}{ega25_25_150-v0004} ordinary
quadratic, it is n and s that the following conditions hold:
1º) \var{\xout{$I/I^2$ is}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_150-v0005} \var{\inserted[typed]{The $gr^{n}_{I}(A)$ are}}{The $gr^{n}_{I}(A)$ are}{insertion}{ega25_25_150-v0006} projective of finite type over A/I.

2º) If d\var{\xout{x}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_150-v0007} denotes the rank of $gr^{1}_{I}(A) = I/I^{2}$ at a $\underline{p} \hand{\in}$Spec(A/I),
then the rank of $gr^{n}_{I}(A)$ at this same point is equal (or simply
$\hand{\geqslant}$) to $\binom{n+d}{d} - \binom{n-2+d}{d}$.

3º) (1º and 2º already imply that $\underline{K}$ = Ker $\underline{\theta}^{\overset{\hand{\unsure{6|\sigma}}}{2}}$ is an invertible
Module locally a direct factor in \var{\deleted{\var{\xout{\illegible{1}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_150-v0009}}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_150-v0008} Sym$^{2}$(I/I$^{2}$)). The sub-Module
$\underline{K}$ = Ker $\theta^{2}$ of Sym$^{2}$(I/I$^{2}$) is nondegenerate.

The proof follows immediately from the following lemma; \var{\deleted{which I
leave you to prove:}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_150-v0010}

\var{\xout{Prop\unsure{osition}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_150-v0011} \uline{Lemma} 8.1. Let B be a ring, M a projective B-module of
finite type, $\hand{\phi} \hand{\in}$ Sym$^{2}$(M) a ``nondegenerate'' element; then multiplication
by $\hand{\phi}$
\[ \mathrm{Sym}^{\overset{\hand{\illegible{1}}}{n\hand{\unsure{-2}}}}(M) \hand{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{Sym}^{n\var{\deleted{\unsure{+2}}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_150-v0012}}(M) \]
is an isomorphism onto a submodule that is a direct factor, so the cokernel
is a projective Module of rank $\binom{n+d}{d} - \binom{n-2+d}{d}$ if M has rank d.

One is immediately reduced to the case where B is the spectrum of a field,
where it is trivial (in fact, ``nondegenerate'' served us only
\var{\margin{||}}{\placedmargin{||}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_150-v0014} to ensure that the $\hand{\phi}(x)$, $x \hand{\in}$ Spec(B), are all $\hand{\neq} 0$, and one could
formulate the lemma more reasonably by replacing 2 by an arbitrary integer
k $\hand{\geqslant}$1, without speaking of nondegeneracy).

\uline{Proposition} 9. Let A be a ring augmented to A/I, with regular
augmentation, I/I$^{2}$ being projective of rank n over A/I. Let E be an A-module

One must express first that the kernel \var{\inserted[typed]{$\underline{K}$}}{$\underline{K}$}{insertion}{ega25_25_154-v0008} of

at x is invertible and a direct factor, i.e. that the homomorphism \unsure{con}\unsure{sid}\unsure{ered}
(which by $x\hand{\in} V^1$ has rank m-1 at x) has exactly rank
\var{\margin{(}}{\placedmargin{(}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_154-v0010} m-1 at x (NB \uline{the rank} of a homomorphism of loc free \unsure{m}odules at a
point is by definition the rank of the corresponding homomorphism of \unsure{v}\unsure{ec}\unsure{t}\unsure{or} spaces over k(x)),
which is expressed by considering
\[ (\hand{\bigwedge}^{m-1} \underline{E})_{V^1}\hand{\to}(\underline{\hand{\Omega}}^{m-1}_{X/\var{\over{S}{Y}}{Y}{writing over}{ega25_25_154-v0011}})_{V^1} \quad , \]
the scheme V'' of zeros of this homomorphism ( $V''\hand{\subset} V^1$ ), and writing

construction explained with Prop. 9\hand{$^{*}$}, one finds \var{\xout{now}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_154-v0015} a homomorphism
\[ M\ : \qquad \underline{K} \hand{\longrightarrow} \underline{\mathrm{Sym}}\var{\xout{m}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_154-v0016}^{2}(\underline{W}) \]
and it remains to express that the latter is ``nondegenerate'' at x. For this,
let us introduce the discriminant
\[ D\ \in\ \hand{\Gamma}\,(V^1-V'',\ \underline{K}^{-n+m\var{\over{\unsure{+|-}}{\unsure{-|+}}}{\unsure{-|+}}{writing over}{ega25_25_154-v0017}1}\otimes \text{dét}(\underline{W})^{2}\ ) \]
(where the exponents denote tensor powers of \unsure{Modules}

that are invertible). Putting $V^2 = V(D)$, which is a closed subprescheme of

\var{\margin{$\|$}}{\placedmargin{$\|$}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_155-v0004} When introducing V", in asserting that $\underline{W}$ and $\underline{K}$ are
locally free on $V^1-V''$, I used a general fact, which I isolate
here as a lemma (where $V^1-V''$ has become X):

\uline{Lemma} Let $v\colon \underline{E} \hand{\to} \underline{F}$ be a homomorphism of locally free Modules
on the prescheme X, \var{\xout{and let}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_155-v0005} m an integer $\hand{>}0$; suppose that $\hand{\bigwedge}^{m} u$ is
zero. \var{\xout{\unsure{(which implies that the rank of u at every point is $\leq$ m) and that}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_155-v0006} \var{\inserted[typed]{Then}}{Then}{insertion}{ega25_25_155-v0007}
$\hand{\bigwedge}^{m-1} u$ vanishes at no point (from the point of view of reduced fibers, of
course) \var{\xout{Then}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_155-v0008} \var{\inserted[typed]{iff}}{iff}{insertion}{ega25_25_155-v0009} u($\underline{E}$) is a sub-Module locally a direct factor of $\underline{F}$,
locally free of rank m-1, \hand{or again iff u has rank \unsure{m}-1 at}
\hand{every pt of X.}

These constructions should be summarized in a proposition
that generalizes Prop. 6. We must see how one can similarly generalize
Prop. 7. For this, suppose that Y itself is smooth over \unsure{a} prescheme
S, \var{\inserted[typed]{of relative dimension N,}}{of relative dimension N,}{insertion}{ega25_25_155-v0010} so X is smooth over S, of relative dimension N+d\unsure{$^{\ast}$}; where d is that of X
over Y. We shall suppose in addition, with the preceding notation, that $V''=\hand{\emptyset}$, i.e.
$\underline{W}$ locally free of rank d-m+1 \var{\inserted[typed]{(this is always the case if m=1!)}}{(this is always the case if m=1!)}{insertion}{ega25_25_155-v0011}. Finally, we shall suppose that the closed
subpreschemes \var{\xout{$V^{\unsure{o}}$}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_155-v0012} \var{\inserted[typed]{$V^o$ and $V^1$}}{$V^o$ and $V^1$}{insertion}{ega25_25_155-v0013} of X are smooth \uline{over} S, of \var{\xout{minimal}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_155-v0014} minimal relative dimension at every
point (for the data d,N,m), \var{\xout{\unsure{which}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_155-v0015} that is, as
one sees immediately, of relative dimensions (N+d) - m and
(N+d) - m - (\unsure{d|n}-\unsure{m|n} +1) = N - 1. (From the point of view of exposition, it
seems best simply to state these numbers outright, perhaps rather in terms
of codimension fiber by fiber, that of $V^o$ in X being m, that of
$V^1$ in $V^o$ being d-m+1; and to point out in a remark the justification
of this choice by the principle of minimal dimension \hand{or} \var{\xout{\unsure{generic}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_155-v0016}

15.3. ``Generalize'' SUP prop.8 to the case of multiplicity n.

15.4. ``Generalize'' SUP prop.9 and cor.10. to the case of multiplicity n.
(These are not really generalizations, but variants..)

15.5. Introduce the notion of an elementary singular zero of multiplicity
n (for n=2, an elementary \unsure{quadra}\unsure{tic} si\unsure{n|g}g\unsure{u|l}\unsure{l|u}ar zero, or an ordinary one) of a
section $\hand{\phi}$ of $\underline{O}_{X}$, or more generally of a locally free Module, on
a locally noetherian X, and the corresponding geometric notion
(over a base field k).

15.6. Let X be a subprescheme of a regular loc noeth prescheme X', and
let x \hand{$\in$}X. For \unsure{x|X} to be an elementary singularity of multiplicity
n of X, it is necessary and sufficient that there be an open neighborhood U of x, and an
$\underline{O}_{U}$-regular sequence ($\hand{\phi}_{1},..,\hand{\phi}_{d}$) such that $X|U = V(\hand{\phi}_{1},..,\hand{\phi}_{d})$ and
such that x is an elementary singular zero of multiplicity n of ($\hand{\phi}_{1}$,..).
In particular, if A is a local noetherian ring that is elementary

\[ v^1 : E\hand{\otimes}\underline{O}_{V^1} \hand{\longrightarrow} \hand{\underline{\Omega}}^1_{X/Y}\hand{\otimes}\underline{O}_{V^1} \]
\var{\xout{in terms of which}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_167-v0001} (itself deduced from the homomorphism of modules

\[ v : \underline{E}\hand{\otimes}\underline{O}_{V^o} \hand{\longrightarrow} \hand{\underline{\Omega}}^1_{X/Y}\hand{\otimes} \underline{O}_{V^o} \quad , \]

1\textsuperscript{o}) that

is precisely $v^1$, which then implies, by the hypothesis that

and that V(u) is also the subprescheme of $V^1$ which makes $\hand{\mu'}$ strictly
of rank \hand{\unsure{$<|\leqslant$}}rank W \var{\deleted{\unsure{$-$}1}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_167-v0006}; on the other hand, one \var{\xout{can also interpret}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_167-v0007} must
verify

2\textsuperscript{o}) that $\hand{\mu'}$ is precisely the homomorphism deduced from the quadratic
form \var{\xout{on}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_167-v0008} M on W with values in K, at the bottom of page 15. It follows
at once that V($\hand{\mu'}$) = V(\unsure{D}) \var{\xout{x}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_167-v0009}, where D is the discriminant of M, which

\RegisterPage{ega25_25_172}{%
% Nouveau EGA V (cote 25): archive cote 25, site page 172 (PDF page 173).

\mspage{\hand{7}}

EGA IV 19

Second thoughts on ``Singular and supersingular set ...'' .

Having just written up the sorites of transversality, I realize that \unsure{the}
context adopted in my notes on singular and \unsure{supersingular} \unsure{sets},
namely sections of loc free Modules, i.e. good vector bundles,
is still not the ``right'' one. If $u$ is a section of a vector bundle
$E = W(\underline{E})$ (associated with $\underline{E}$ loc free of finite type) over X smooth over Y, then $V(u)$
is simply the inverse image \unsure{of the} \var{\inserted[typed]{subprescheme $E_{o}$ of $E$}}{subprescheme $E_{o}$ of $E$}{insertion}{ega25_25_172-v0004} ``zero section'', and a point $x\hand{\in} V(u)$
is nonsingular \var{\inserted[typed]{for u}}{for u}{insertion}{ega25_25_172-v0005} rel. to S iff u is \uline{transverse} to $E_{o}$ at x rel. to Y.
If this condition is not satisfied, i.e. if x is singular for u rel to
Y, we study the conditions under which x is not too singular
rel. to Y, i.e. u does not deviate too far from transversality at x. I have
no doubt that all the developments in my notes, with essentially
trivial changes, extend to the case where one has an X-prescheme E, a
subprescheme $E_{o}$ of E, a section u of E over X, and considers the inverse
image $X_{o}$ of $E_{o}$ under u, \var{\inserted[typed]{assuming E and $E_{o}$ smooth over X at the points of $v(X)$.}}{assuming E and $E_{o}$ smooth over X at the points of $v(X)$.}{insertion}{ega25_25_172-v0008} it is possible (but \unsure{only} a detailed
account will enable one to detect this) that it will sometimes be necessary to assume that
the relative dimension of $E_{o}$ over X at the points of $v(X_{o})$ is zero, i.e. that $E_{o}$ is
even étale over X at these points (which will be the case when $E_{o}$ comes, as
above, from a section of E over X, say $v_{o}$). Thus, x will be a point
``\var{\xout{singular}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_172-v0011} \var{\inserted[typed]{of nontransversality to $E_{o}$}}{of nontransversality to $E_{o}$}{insertion}{ega25_25_172-v0012} that is ordinary for v, relative to Y'' if and only if \var{\inserted[typed]{$x$}}{$x$}{insertion}{ega25_25_172-v0013} \var{\deleted{$\illegible{1}_{oy}$}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_172-v0014} \var{\inserted{$x$}}{$x$}{insertion}{ega25_25_172-v0015} is
geometrically an ordinary quadratic point of $X_{o\,y}$ , and if $\mathrm{codim}_{x}(X_{oy},X_{y})$
$= c$ , where c is the codimension of $E_{o}$ in E (at $v(x)$) ; this implies that
$X_{o}\hand{\longrightarrow} X$ is \var{\inserted{an imm.}}{an imm.}{insertion}{ega25_25_172-v0016} transversely regular at x rel. to Y .... The role of the Module
$\underline{E}\hand{\otimes}\underline{O}_{V(u)}$ will here be played by $v_{o}^{\hand{*}}(\underline{N}_{E_{o}/E})$ , where $v_{o}:X_{o}\hand{\longrightarrow} E_{o}$ is induced by v. I
think you will have no trouble writing everything in this context, which is much more
natural after all---with the translations to the vector bundle case
left to the end. If there are difficulties even in getting started, we
could work on them \unsure{to}\unsure{gether} when you next pass through Paris ... \hand{I shall send you brief notes in the next few days.}
\var{\margin{\hand{172}}}{\placedmargin{\hand{172}}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_172-v0018}
\tnote{25-172-1}{The doubts in the, sets, supersingular and of the retain respectively the French e/r, h/l, final s and a/u uncertainties. Only retains the s/g doubt in seul; the two parts of together retain the e/t and b/v doubts in ensemble. The canceled s in the article les, the doubly canceled la, the isolated canceled f and the feminine e in régulière have no separate English effect. The canceled fragment d\unsure{e|u} remains doubtful. Within the inserted clause, the overwritten old \unsure{O|e} and \unsure{ant} likewise have no English spelling effect.}
\tnote{25-172-2}{Loc means locally; rel. means relative; sss is rendered iff; imm. is retained for immersion. The words that is allow ordinary to follow the inserted complement in English while point remains outside the insertion. The source first says S and then Y, changes from u to v, uses the two displayed occurrences of x in succession, and uses the indicated meanings of the subscripted v; these readings are retained.}

\RegisterPage{ega25_25_174}{%
% Nouveau EGA V (cote 25): archive cote 25, site page 174 (PDF page 175).

\var{\margin{\unsure{IV|1/U}}}{\placedmargin{\unsure{IV|1/U}}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_174-v0001} \var{\margin{\hand{new EGA V}}}{\placedmargin{\hand{new EGA V}}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_174-v0002} \mspage{\hand{1}}

17.16. \uline{Smooth quadratic forms}.

16.1.Let $Q$ be \unsure{a|6} section of $\underline{Sym}^2(\underline{E})$, ($\underline{E}$ loc free of finite rank),
so that Q \var{\xout{defines}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_174-v0003} (which can also be interpreted as a quadratic
form on $\overset{\hand{\vee}}{\underline{E}}$ ) \var{\xout{\unsure{or} again as a section}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_174-v0004} defines a symmetric bilinear
form B on $\overset{\hand{\vee}}{\underline{E}}$, hence a homomorphism $\overset{\hand{\vee}}{\underline{E}} \hand{\longrightarrow} \underline{E}$ , and passing to the
determinant Modules one finds $\text{dét}\ \overset{\hand{\vee}}{\underline{E}} \hand{\longrightarrow} \det \underline{E}$ , hence finally a section
\[ d(Q) \hand{\in} \hand{\Gamma}(\ \text{dét}\ (E)^{\hand{\otimes} 2}) \]
called (unless I am mistaken) the \uline{discriminant of the quadratic form} Q. When
$\underline{E} = \underline{O}_S^{\ \unsure{n|m}}$ , it is simply the section of $\underline{O}_S$ given by the determinant of the matrix
with n rows and n columns, with coeff in $\hand{\Gamma}\underline{O}_S$ , which expresses Q . Let us note
at once:

\uline{Proposition} 16.2. Suppose that for every $s \hand{\in} S$, we have char $k(s) \hand{\neq} 2$ \uline{or}
rank $E\hand{\otimes} k(s)$ even. Then, for Q to be smooth, it is necessary and sufficient that Q be
``nondegenerate'', i.e. that d(Q) be invertible. \hand{(}Moreover, the condition is
sufficient without restriction on S or $\underline{E}$\hand{)}.

The last assertion is included only for the convenience of possible
references, since it is trivially contained in the first one:
the hypothesis that Q is nondegenerate indeed implies that $\underline{E}$ has even rank
at every point whose char is 2. M\hand{\raisebox{.7ex}{\unsure{+|t}}}oreover, it can be proved directly
without considering the characteristic, since (working over an
\var{\inserted{alg closed}}{alg closed}{insertion}{ega25_25_174-v0005} field and taking a basis) it expresses that the $\frac{\hand{\partial} Q}{\hand{\partial} X_i}$ have no nontrivial common zero\var{\xout{s}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_174-v0006}
and a fortiori \unsure{they} have no nontrivial common zero with Q.
If char $k \hand{\neq} 2$, the converse is true, since by the formula
\[ 2Q = \hand{\sum} X_i \frac{\hand{\partial} Q}{\hand{\partial} X_i} \]
one then sees that every common zero of the $\frac{\hand{\partial} \unsure{Q|E}}{\hand{\partial} X_i}$ is also a zero of Q. Finally,
if char $k = \unsure{2}$ , \var{\xout{if E has even rank}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_174-v0008} then the bilinear form B

\var{\margin{\hand{174}}}{\placedmargin{\hand{174}}}{marginal note placed}{ega25_25_174-v0009}

The canceled plural ending of zéros is retained in zero(s); the separate adjective-agreement s in communs has no English counterpart.}

For every integer $n\hand{>}0$, let us introduce the ``standard quadratic form''
$Q_n$ on $\underline{Z}^n$ , as a form with integer coefficients in n variables
$X_1,..,X_n$ , distinguishing the two cases:
a) $n = 2m$ , $Q_{2m}(X_1,..,X_{2m}) = X_1X_2 + X_3X_4 + \ldots$
b) $n = 2m+1$, $Q_{2m+1}(X_1,..,X_{2m+1}) =$\var{\xout{\unsure{$(X_1^{2}X_2+X$}}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_175-v0010} $Q_{2m}(X_1,..,X_{2m}) + X_{2m+1}^2$.

\uline{Corollary} 16.10. Let k be a field, E a vector space of finite dimension
over k, $Q \hand{\in} \mathrm{Sym}^2(E)$. Equivalent conditions:

(i) Q is smooth.

(ii) $\overset{\hand{\sim}}{d}(Q) \hand{\neq} 0$.

(iii) There is a \var{\xout{finite}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_178-v0001} extension k' of k such that $Q\hand{\otimes} k'$ is
isomorphic to the standard form.

(iii bis) As in (iii), with k' a finite extension of k.

This is a trivial consequence of 16.9. Note that when k is
algebraically closed, (iii) and (iii bis) are replaced by the
more striking condition: Q is isomorphic to the standard form.

Proof of 16.9. We \var{\xout{obviously have}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_178-v0002} can obviously
suppose E of constant rank n. We shall obviously have
\[ \text{(iii bis)} \hand{\Longrightarrow} \text{(iii)} \hand{\Longrightarrow} \text{(ii)} \]
given that for the standard form the modified discriminant is 1.
We shall now prove (ii)\hand{$\Longrightarrow$}(iii bis), then (i)\hand{$\Longleftrightarrow$}(ii).

Let $\underline{E}_o = \underline{O}_S^{\ n}$ , $Q_o$ the standard form on $\underline{E}_o$ . Consider the
functor
\[ \underline{\mathrm{Isom}}( (\underline{E}_o,Q_o),(\underline{E},Q)) :\ (\mathrm{Sch})_{/S}^{\ o} \hand{\longrightarrow} (\mathrm{Ens}) , \]
whose value at every S' over S consists of the set of isomorphisms
$\underline{E}_{o\,S'} \hand{\to} \underline{E}_{S'}$ compatible with the forms $Q_{o\,S'}$ and $Q_{S'}$ . It is immediate
(without any condition on \var{\inserted{$\underline{E}$ or}}{$\underline{E}$ or}{insertion}{ega25_25_178-v0003} Q) that this functor is representable by a prescheme
P affine and of finite presentation over S, which is a \var{\inserted[typed]{sub}}{sub}{insertion}{ega25_25_178-v0004}\unsure{pre}scheme of W =
$W(\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\underline{O}_S}(\underline{E}_o,\underline{E}))$ , and a closed subprescheme of \var{\deleted{$\underline{\mathrm{Isom}}(\underline{E}$}}{}{deletion}{ega25_25_178-v0005} the open
$\underline{\mathrm{Isom}}\ (\underline{E}_o,\underline{E}_1)$ of W \hand{/}. The implication (ii)\hand{$\Longrightarrow$}(iii bis) will be proved if
we show that when $\overset{\hand{\sim}}{d}(Q)$ is invertible, P is faithfully flat
over S: we shall indeed take S'=P.

For simplicity, set \var{\xout{\unsure{$\underline{G}(\underline{E}$}x}}{}{typewriter strike-out}{ega25_25_178-v0006}\hand{$_{\unsure{Q|o}}$}

\section*{Text, provenance, and rights}
AI-transcribed by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic, effort high, Message Batches API); checked against the scans, and this edition built, by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode); prompts and records by Claude (Anthropic).

AI-translated by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode).

Cote 25 is described in the archive as dated ``[à partir de 1967-1987]''. The source of each reading is the attached Montpellier scan. The named published texts---the Grothendieck Circle scan EGA5.pdf, the P. and J. Blass translations (2004), J. C. Reinhold's web re-edition, and the Centre for Grothendieckian Studies item L49d---are not reproduced and have not been consulted for any reading.

The rights in the original work belong to its author or the author's representatives or heirs. Where we hold rights, in the AI-produced transcription, translation, corrections and typesetting, they are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0. This edition is published for educational, non-profit purposes, and we claim no rights we do not hold. If you hold rights in this work and object to its publication here, please open a GitHub issue and we will take it down.

\clearpage\section*{How to read this edition}
The diplomatic form follows archive order. The corrected and reading forms for cote 25 order the material as IV 16, IV 17.15--17.16, IV 20, and IV 21, followed by the letter to Dieudonné. Interleaved leaves are retained with the relevant groups. Cote 24 keeps its archive order; its stray curriculum-vitae leaf at site 76 appears in the diplomatic form only.

Handwriting is blue in the diplomatic form, manuscript deletions red, and typewriter strike-outs gray. Angle brackets mark insertions, and a small rising arrow marks writing over typed text. The corrected form incorporates the additions and replacements and records each difference in the apparatus. The reading form omits the apparatus and its editorial reference marks. Source marginal notes, unresolved readings, and translator queries remain.

The new English translation follows the supplied unified glossary. The mathematical formulas retain the token strings of the mechanically cleaned corrected French text. Translation explanations are confined to translator's notes. The English annotated master preserves the French variant identifiers.

Every scan mark and every uncertainty or illegibility mark links to the corresponding page in the Montpellier viewer. The original page numbers remain distinct from this volume's pagination.
